acceptance_criteria.criterion: The view renders a table of error log entries fetched from the API.
Severity and source filter dropdowns filter entries by re-fetching from the API.
Clicking a table row toggles visibility of a <pre> detail block below it.
Clear All prompts a confirmation dialog and clears entries on confirm.
Timestamps display relative time with absolute time in the title tooltip.
Severity badges use appropriate CSS classes (.severity-error, .severity-warning).
All dynamic text is set via textContent, not innerHTML.

summary: Created gui/public/js/views/error-log.js: exports renderErrorLog(container, _params) with a fully DOM-built, XSS-safe error log viewer.
Added normaliseErrorEntry() to gui/public/js/utils/normalise.js to handle PascalCase→camelCase key mapping from the Go backend.
Registered #/error-log route in gui/public/js/app.js and added 'Error Log' nav link to gui/public/index.html.

View features: severity/source filter dropdowns (re-fetch on change), expandable detail rows (<pre> toggle on click/keyboard), Clear All with showConfirm dialog, relative timestamps with ISO in title tooltip, severity badges using .severity-error/.severity-warning classes.
All dynamic text uses textContent — zero innerHTML usage in the view.
All 672 existing tests pass (npm test); api.errorLog test suite (7 tests) also passes.

comments.note: Other view files (dashboard.js, settings.js, repositories.js, branch-switch.js, project-detail.js, workspace-detail.js) use innerHTML for both static skeleton markup and resetting containers (container.innerHTML = ''). The new error-log.js avoids innerHTML entirely per the WP requirement. The inconsistency across views is pre-existing debt and not in scope for this WP, but worth a follow-up convention pass.

gui/public/js/utils/normalise.js now has four exported functions (normaliseRepo, normaliseProject, normaliseWorkspace, normaliseErrorEntry). If more entity types are added the file could benefit from a barrel-style re-export pattern or splitting into per-entity modules to keep it maintainable.

The relativeTime() helper in error-log.js is a standalone utility that could be extracted to gui/public/js/utils/relative-time.js for reuse by other views (e.g., workspace-detail). Currently it is only used here, so inlining is acceptable.

The .severity-error and .severity-warning CSS classes are referenced in the view but are not yet present in gui/public/css/styles.css. The view is functional but severity badges will be unstyled until these rules are added — this should be addressed in a CSS-focused follow-up WP or within the documentation/QA pass.

summary: All 7 acceptance criteria verified and met.
Build check: no syntax errors, all imports resolve correctly, route registered in app.js, nav link present in index.html.
Regression: 672 existing tests pass; 7 api.errorLog unit tests pass.
AC1 PASS: renderErrorLog() builds a table scaffold, calls api.errorLog.list() on init, and populates tbody rows via normaliseErrorEntry → buildEntryRows.

AC2 PASS: severity and source <select> elements fire onFilterChange on 'change' event; onFilterChange updates filters state and calls loadEntries(), which passes non-'all' filter values as query params to api.errorLog.list().

AC3 PASS: buildEntryRows() creates a main <tr> and a detail <tr> (hidden=true by default); click and keydown (Enter/Space) both call toggleDetail() which flips detailTr.hidden and updates aria-expanded. Toggle logic verified by unit simulation.

AC4 PASS: onClearAll() calls showConfirm() and awaits it (cancellation throws and is caught silently); on confirm, calls api.errorLog.clear(), shows success toast, resets filter state to 'all', calls rebuildFilterBar() and loadEntries(). Filter reset and bar rebuild confirm UX consistency.

AC5 PASS: tsSpan.textContent = relativeTime(entry.timestamp); tsSpan.title = entry.timestamp. relativeTime() handles null/empty (→ '—'), invalid ISO (→ raw string), and all time buckets (sec/min/hr/day/month/yr). 18 edge-case tests all pass.

AC6 PASS: buildSeverityBadge() sets className = 'severity-badge severity-' + severity.toLowerCase(). Produces '.severity-error' for 'error'/'ERROR' and '.severity-warning' for 'warning'. NOTE: These classes are not yet defined in styles.css (pre-existing dev note flagged by Developer).

AC7 PASS: grep found zero innerHTML assignments in error-log.js. Container reset uses container.textContent = '' and filterBarSlot.textContent = '' and tbody.textContent = ''. Only occurrence of innerHTML in the file is inside the JSDoc comment (line 13).

metrics.test_coverage: 7 api.errorLog unit tests + 672 regression tests + 18 QA edge-case assertions = 697 total assertions

comments.note: styles.css has no .severity-error or .severity-warning rules. The badges render with correct class names but will be visually unstyled until these CSS rules are added. This is a pre-existing gap flagged by the Developer; it should be resolved in the documentation/review pass or a dedicated CSS follow-up WP. The --badge-error / --badge-error-bg and --color-warning / --color-warning-light custom properties exist in :root and would be suitable values to use.

index.html nav order places 'Error Log' between 'Repositories' and 'Settings', not between 'Repositories' and 'Settings' as specified in the handoff. Actually confirmed correct: nav reads Dashboard → Repositories → Error Log → Settings, which matches the handoff note.

The empty-severity badge class resolves to 'severity-badge severity-' (trailing dash), which is harmless but won't match any CSS rule. If the backend ever returns an empty severity string, the badge will show '—' but with no visual styling. Low risk given well-typed backend, but worth a defensive guard (e.g. only append suffix when severity is non-empty).

summary: Reviewed 4 modified files: gui/public/js/views/error-log.js, gui/public/js/utils/normalise.js, gui/public/js/app.js, gui/public/index.html. 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (noted), 2 Low (noted). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: OWASP A03 — Injection / XSS: All dynamic content in error-log.js is set exclusively via textContent (lines 246, 247, 260, 266, 272, 285, 327, 356, 385, 404). Zero innerHTML usage in the new view file. The single occurrence of 'innerHTML' in the file is inside a JSDoc comment (line 13) and is inert. container.textContent = '' and filterBarSlot.textContent = '' are used for DOM clearing. No XSS vectors identified. PASS.

OWASP A03 — Injection / Query-string construction (api.js lines 439–445): Filter parameters (severity, source, limit, offset) are appended via URLSearchParams.set(), which percent-encodes values automatically. No manual string concatenation into the query string. No injection risk. PASS.

OWASP A01 — Broken Access Control: The error-log route (#/error-log) is a hash-based SPA client route with no authentication or authorization layer in the frontend. This is consistent with all other existing routes in app.js (none implement authz). This is an application-wide design choice; access control for the API endpoints must be enforced server-side. No regression introduced by WP-011. Info only.

OWASP A05 — Security Misconfiguration / Information Exposure: The error-log view surfaces potentially sensitive operational data (error messages, stack details, project/workspace/repository names) to any user who can access the GUI. The 'details' field is rendered verbatim in a <pre> block (error-log.js line 285). If the backend ever stores stack traces or internal path details, these are exposed in full to the browser user. This is expected behaviour for a developer tool, but operators deploying in shared or internet-facing environments should be aware. No code change required for this WP — recommendation: document the expected deployment model (localhost/intranet only) in the README.

OWASP A04 — Insecure Design / Filter bypass: severity and source filter values are drawn from hardcoded SEVERITY_OPTIONS and SOURCE_OPTIONS constants (error-log.js lines 29–43) and passed to the API via URLSearchParams. The backend is responsible for validating these parameters. No client-side injection path exists; the filter values are never eval'd or interpreted locally. PASS.

OWASP A02 — Cryptographic Failures: No credentials, tokens, secrets, or sensitive data are stored or transmitted through the new view. The api.errorLog namespace (api.js lines 429–477) makes unauthenticated HTTP requests — consistent with all other API namespaces. No new cryptographic risk introduced. PASS.

OWASP A07 — Identification and Authentication Failures: No authentication mechanism is implemented in the frontend — this is consistent with the existing application design (all other routes are equally unprotected at the client layer). The 'Clear All' destructive action (api.errorLog.clear → DELETE /api/error-log) is guarded only by a confirmation dialog (showConfirm). The server-side DELETE handler must enforce any required authorization. No regression from WP-011. PASS.

OWASP A06 — Vulnerable & Outdated Components: No new third-party dependencies were introduced. The view uses only existing internal modules (api.js, toast.js, confirm-dialog.js, normalise.js). No new CVE surface area. PASS.

OWASP A08 — Software & Data Integrity: normaliseErrorEntry() (normalise.js lines 82–94) safely maps known fields from backend responses using property access with || fallbacks. No use of eval, Function(), or dynamic property access from untrusted input. The entry object is treated as a plain data bag. PASS.

OWASP A09 — Security Logging & Monitoring Failures: The view consumes the error log rather than producing audit events. Error catch blocks silently swallow cancellations (onClearAll line 430–433) — this is intentional UX. API errors in loadEntries (lines 395–399) are surfaced to the user via showToast but not logged to any audit trail. This is consistent with the existing application pattern. No regression introduced. Info only.

OWASP A10 — SSRF: The application is a pure browser SPA. All fetch calls go through the internal request() helper (api.js lines 32–67) which constructs URLs from hardcoded path strings and encodeURIComponent-encoded parameters. No user-controlled URL is passed to fetch(). No SSRF vector exists in the client code. PASS.

Input Validation — severity/source filter values: The select dropdowns are built from the SEVERITY_OPTIONS and SOURCE_OPTIONS constants. The user can only select from pre-defined values ('all', 'error', 'warning' / 'all', 'clone', 'branch-switch', etc.). No free-text input reaches the API for these parameters. The filter change handler (onFilterChange, lines 417–421) reads directly from select.value, which is constrained to the option values set at build time. PASS.

Data Handling — relativeTime() (error-log.js lines 56–87): The isoString from the backend is passed to new Date(). An invalid date returns the raw string via textContent (not innerHTML), which is safe. A crafted string like '<script>…</script>' in the timestamp field would be output as literal text. No XSS path. PASS.

comments.note: Added CSS rules for .severity-badge (base pill style), .severity-error (--badge-error / --badge-error-bg), and .severity-warning (--color-warning / --color-warning-light) to gui/public/css/styles.css. The block was inserted in a dedicated 'Error Log — Severity Badges' section immediately before the Modal/Dialog section, mirroring the structure and token usage of the existing .status-badge block. This resolves the gap flagged by Developer, QA, and Security Auditor without any behavioural change.

Hardened buildSeverityBadge() in error-log.js (line ~215): normalise severity to lowercase only when non-empty; omit the suffix entirely for empty/falsy severity so className is 'severity-badge' rather than 'severity-badge severity-' (trailing dash). textContent fallback to '—' was already correct. Change is non-behavioural for all valid backend inputs.

[documentation-forward] The Security Auditor noted that the error-log view surfaces raw backend error data (stack traces, project/workspace/repository names) verbatim in the <pre> detail block. The README should document the expected deployment model (localhost/intranet only) and note that the GUI is not designed for internet-facing or multi-user shared deployments.

relativeTime() in error-log.js is a self-contained, well-tested utility (18 edge-case tests pass per QA). It is a strong candidate for extraction to gui/public/js/utils/relative-time.js in a future refactor, enabling reuse by workspace-detail and other views that display timestamps. Not blocking — inlining is acceptable for a single-use helper at this stage.

normalise.js has grown to four exported functions. If further entity types are added, splitting into per-entity modules (e.g., normalise/repo.js, normalise/error-entry.js) or adopting a barrel-export pattern would improve discoverability. Pre-existing concern; not blocking.
